text:
Maya: quick async standup — what I did: merged the prefetch heuristic prototype (PR #432). ran a few microbench suites against gpunode-3 and saw steady throughput but p99 spikes at ~420ms for 4k seqs.
Maya: blocker: KV warmup not hitting >85% hit-rate on cold flows, looks like our prefix hashing misses some repeated tokens. also seen a couple of OOMs in the canary with 8 concurrent streams.
Maya: today: iterate on prefix hashing, add a lightweight metric to track unique prefix buckets, and re-run the p99 matrix. will also open a short rollback option on the canary.

Sam: nice work on the heuristic — do you have the perf numbers posted? can we see the microbench diff vs main?
Sam: if it's a kernel-level mem pattern causing the p99, might be worth turning on the new allocator patch in dev to compare.

Maya: pasted the microbench csv to the perf board, link: https://redwood.tools/perf/1951234567 (perm: eng-runtime). diff vs main: +3% throughput, -6% median latency, +18% p99 for 4k.

Lin: quick thought — KV warmup hit-rate can be improved by a small LRU pre-seed for hot prefixes. I prototyped something last quarter, can rebase and drop it in. low risk.

Pete: ping on the OOMs — what errors in the logs? do we have the exact stack?

Maya: logs had `cudaMemcpy` OOM traces, memory usage peaked right after a large microbatch flush. suspect bursty KV prefetch combined with batching. stack snippet: ```
E 03-17 09:12:45 cudaMemcpy failed: out of memory
  at runtime/kernel/allocator.cc:412
  at runtime/batcher.cc:128
```

Anika: FYI deploy-bot reported the canary deploy succeeded earlier then a rollout pause at 09:20 when health check failed. deploy-bot: "canary: pg-4 - paused due to 2 failing healthchecks" :warning:", maybe related.

deploy-bot: canary status: pg-4 deploy v1.7.3 — paused at 1951234720 due to healthcheck failures (2/5). See /deploys/pg-4 for logs.

Sam: can you try running the microbench with `--no-prefetch` to confirm prefetched KV is the main contributor? small command:
```
./bench/microbench --seq-len 4096 --concurrency 8 --repeat 50 --prefetch=off
```

Maya: running that now, will post results in ~20m.

Lin: if `--no-prefetch` improves p99, we should gate the heuristic behind a runtime flag and do gradual ramp. also add a tiny buffer pool to avoid OOM when prefetch triggers concurrently.

Pete: I'll take a look at the allocator trace and see if a fast-path can return pages earlier. assigning to me: investigate allocator free latency. ETA EOD.

Anika: I'll coordinate with infra to increase canary memory headroom temporarily to get more stable runs. also will schedule a quick sync at 11:30 if folks prefer a live triage.

Maya: thanks all — action items: Lin to rebase LRU pre-seed (low-risk), Pete to investigate allocator frees, Anika to bump canary memory + schedule 11:30 triage, Sam to run `--no-prefetch` bench, Maya to push metric for prefix buckets and re-run p99 matrix.

Sam: acked, will run bench and drop numbers here. :thumbsup:

Lin: ack, will open PR draft today and link in this thread.

Pete: ack, will post a short patch if I find a cheap free-path.

Anika: ack, created a temporary ticket INFRA-947 and increased canary memory by 10% for pg-4.

Maya: FYI if someone wants to review PR #433 (tiny exporter for prefix buckets), it needs 1 reviewer. CC @Sam.

Sam: quick review pass in a bit.

Maya: final note — if anyone sees regression on cost per token after changes, call it out. we should prefer a modest latency win without 2x mem.

Maya: signing off for now, will update after bench run.
